text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Moi says ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU) will amend its constitution to reinstate a clause allowing expulsion of dissident members.
- Fifty lawyers owe the Nairobi City Council about one billion shillings which they collected on behalf of city hall.
- Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae says the Agricultural Finance Corporation will not be privatised.
- The Electoral Commission has altered boundaries of various parliamentary constituencies in 24 districts.
- Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem says the bank will not lower the cash ratio just to help bring interest rates down.
- Several traders in Nairobi say mushrooming of so-called "trade exhibitions" is unfair competition with shopkeepers.
- The second largest beer company in the country, Kuguru Food Complex, accuses local liquor firms of using dubious ways to defraud the government of millions of shillings by not paying excise duty.
